- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.75) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) or negative, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 72.5), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.  
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 5% below recent 10-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; if sentiment turns negative within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 2–4% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating high/low cycles, model tends to lag; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
